newsitem.title: USA: Barringer sees record Q4 detector sales.
newsitem.headline: Barringer sees record Q4 detector sales.

text.p: Barringer Technologies Inc said Tuesday it shipped a record number of its airport bomb and drug detection systems in the fourth quarter and expects to report record sales as a result.
The company said it expects to report record sales for both the fourth quarter and 1996 year.

Reached by phone, Chief Executive Stanley Binder said the company's previous record for bomb detector sales had been set in the third quarter ended September 1996, when the company had net sales of $2.3 million. Virtually all Barringer's overall sales derive from its bomb detector business, he said.
The company's trace particle drug and explosives detection system is known as IONSCAN.

In a statement, the company said that among the sales recorded for the quarter were a substantial number of IONSCANs delivered to an overseas customer for narcotics applications, the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), and the completion of shipments made under the company's previously announced contract with the European Passenger Services Ltd.

It said a number of the security systems delivered to the FAA will be deployed by major airlines while others will be delivered to the FAA to further develop test protocols and operational procedures.
In the statement, Binder said that, "The record orders reflect widespread acceptance of the IONSCAN, both from drug and explosives detection."
"We are gratified by the wide-spread market acceptance of our products and look forward to another successful year in 1997."
